mission: CAIS (pronounced 'case') is a San Francisco research and field-building nonprofit. Its mission is to reduce societal-scale risks from AI by doing safety research, building the field of AI safety researchers (courses, fellowships, a free compute cluster), and advocating for safety standards.

key_work.title: Statement on AI Risk
key_work.plain_summary: One sentence signed by hundreds of AI leaders: mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside pandemics and nuclear war.

key_work.title: An Overview of Catastrophic AI Risks
key_work.plain_summary: Sorts AI catastrophe into malicious use, AI races, organisational accidents and rogue AI.

key_work.title: Humanity's Last Exam
key_work.plain_summary: Thousands of expert-written questions at the edge of human knowledge, built (with Scale AI) to test frontier models.

key_work.title: The WMDP Benchmark: Measuring and Reducing Malicious Use With Unlearning
key_work.plain_summary: Tests hazardous bio, chem and cyber knowledge in models and shows a way to remove it.

key_work.title: Superintelligence Strategy (MAIM)
key_work.plain_summary: With Eric Schmidt and Alexandr Wang: states could deter rivals from racing to superintelligence through 'Mutual Assured AI Malfunction'.

key_work.title: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMLU)
key_work.plain_summary: Dan Hendrycks's widely used knowledge benchmark across 57 subjects.

key_work.title: Representation Engineering
key_work.plain_summary: Reads and steers high-level concepts such as honesty directly in a model's internal activity.

warnings.text: AI carries risks that are potentially catastrophic, including malicious use, competitive pressure and loss of control.
Many basic problems in AI safety remain unsolved despite dramatic AI progress.
Frontier models already hold hazardous knowledge (for example in virology) that could help bad actors.

recommendations.text: Treat AI extinction risk as a global priority.
Take a multidisciplinary approach across academia, government, companies and the public.
Build the safety research field with courses, fellowships and shared compute.
Advocate for safety standards and deterrence among states racing for superintelligence.
